18.12: Anyone who does these things is detestable to the Lord. It is because the other nations have done these detestable things that the Lord your God will drive them out ahead of you.
18.13: But you must be blameless before the Lord your God.
18.14: The nations you are about to displace consult sorcerers and fortune-tellers, but the Lord your God forbids you to do such things.”
18.15: Moses continued, “The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your fellow Israelites. You must listen to him.
18.16: For this is what you yourselves requested of the Lord your God when you were assembled at Mount Sinai. You said, ‘Don’t let us hear the voice of the Lord our God anymore or see this blazing fire, for we will die.’
18.17: “Then the Lord said to me, ‘What they have said is right.
18.18: I will raise up a prophet like you from among their fellow Israelites. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell the people everything I command him.
18.19: I will personally deal with anyone who will not listen to the messages the prophet proclaims on my behalf.
18.20: But any prophet who falsely claims to speak in my name or who speaks in the name of another god must die.’
18.21: “But you may wonder, ‘How will we know whether or not a prophecy is from the Lord?’
18.22: If the prophet speaks in the Lord’s name but his prediction does not happen or come true, you will know that the Lord did not give that message. That prophet has spoken without my authority and need not be feared.

8.1: “Be careful to obey all the commands I am giving you today. Then you will live and multiply, and you will enter and occupy the land the Lord swore to give your ancestors.
8.2: Remember how the Lord your God led you through the wilderness for these forty years, humbling you and testing you to prove your character, and to find out whether or not you would obey his commands.
8.3: Yes, he humbled you by letting you go hungry and then feeding you with manna, a food previously unknown to you and your ancestors. He did it to teach you that people do not live by bread alone; rather, we live by every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord.
8.4: For all these forty years your clothes didn’t wear out, and your feet didn’t blister or swell.
8.5: Think about it: Just as a parent disciplines a child, the Lord your God disciplines you for your own good.
8.6: “So obey the commands of the Lord your God by walking in his ways and fearing him.
8.7: For the Lord your God is bringing you into a good land of flowing streams and pools of water, with fountains and springs that gush out in the valleys and hills.
8.8: It is a land of wheat and barley; of grapevines, fig trees, and pomegranates; of olive oil and honey.
8.9: It is a land where food is plentiful and nothing is lacking. It is a land where iron is as common as stone, and copper is abundant in the hills.
8.10: When you have eaten your fill, be sure to praise the Lord your God for the good land he has given you.
8.11: “But that is the time to be careful! Beware that in your plenty you do not forget the Lord your God and disobey his commands, regulations, and decrees that I am giving you today.
8.12: For when you have become full and prosperous and have built fine homes to live in,
8.13: and when your flocks and herds have become very large and your silver and gold have multiplied along with everything else, be careful!
8.14: Do not become proud at that time and forget the Lord your God, who rescued you from slavery in the land of Egypt.
8.15: Do not forget that he led you through the great and terrifying wilderness with its poisonous snakes and scorpions, where it was so hot and dry. He gave you water from the rock!
8.16: He fed you with manna in the wilderness, a food unknown to your ancestors. He did this to humble you and test you for your own good.
8.17: He did all this so you would never say to yourself, ‘I have achieved this wealth with my own strength and energy.’
8.18: Remember the Lord your God. He is the one who gives you power to be successful, in order to fulfill the covenant he confirmed to your ancestors with an oath.
8.19: “But I assure you of this: If you ever forget the Lord your God and follow other gods, worshiping and bowing down to them, you will certainly be destroyed.
8.20: Just as the Lord has destroyed other nations in your path, you also will be destroyed if you refuse to obey the Lord your God.

34.1: Then Moses went up to Mount Nebo from the plains of Moab and climbed Pisgah Peak, which is across from Jericho. And the Lord showed him the whole land, from Gilead as far as Dan
34.2: all the land of Naphtali; the land of Ephraim and Manasseh; all the land of Judah, extending to the Mediterranean Sea
34.3: the Negev; the Jordan Valley with Jericho—the city of palms—as far as Zoar.
34.4: Then the Lord said to Moses, “This is the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ I have now allowed you to see it with your own eyes, but you will not enter the land.”
34.5: So Moses, the servant of the Lord, died there in the land of Moab, just as the Lord had said.
34.6: The Lord buried him in a valley near Beth-peor in Moab, but to this day no one knows the exact place.
34.7: Moses was 120 years old when he died, yet his eyesight was clear, and he was as strong as ever.
34.8: The people of Israel mourned for Moses on the plains of Moab for thirty days, until the customary period of mourning was over.
34.9: Now Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him. So the people of Israel obeyed him, doing just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
34.10: There has never been another prophet in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face.
34.11: The Lord sent him to perform all the miraculous signs and wonders in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh, and all his servants, and his entire land.
34.12: With mighty power, Moses performed terrifying acts in the sight of all Israel.

22.1: “If you see your neighbor’s ox or sheep or goat wandering away, don’t ignore your responsibility. Take it back to its owner.
22.2: If its owner does not live nearby or you don’t know who the owner is, take it to your place and keep it until the owner comes looking for it. Then you must return it.
22.3: Do the same if you find your neighbor’s donkey, clothing, or anything else your neighbor loses. Don’t ignore your responsibility.
22.4: “If you see that your neighbor’s donkey or ox has collapsed on the road, do not look the other way. Go and help your neighbor get it back on its feet!
22.5: “A woman must not put on men’s clothing, and a man must not wear women’s clothing. Anyone who does this is detestable in the sight of the Lord your God.
22.6: “If you happen to find a bird’s nest in a tree or on the ground, and there are young ones or eggs in it with the mother sitting in the nest, do not take the mother with the young.
22.7: You may take the young, but let the mother go, so that you may prosper and enjoy a long life.
22.8: “When you build a new house, you must build a railing around the edge of its flat roof. That way you will not be considered guilty of murder if someone falls from the roof.
22.9: “You must not plant any other crop between the rows of your vineyard. If you do, you are forbidden to use either the grapes from the vineyard or the other crop.
22.10: “You must not plow with an ox and a donkey harnessed together.
22.11: “You must not wear clothing made of wool and linen woven together.
22.12: “You must put four tassels on the hem of the cloak with which you cover yourself—on the front, back, and sides.
22.13: “Suppose a man marries a woman, but after sleeping with her, he turns against her
22.14: and publicly accuses her of shameful conduct, saying, ‘When I married this woman, I discovered she was not a virgin.’
22.15: Then the woman’s father and mother must bring the proof of her virginity to the elders as they hold court at the town gate.
22.16: Her father must say to them, ‘I gave my daughter to this man to be his wife, and now he has turned against her.
22.17: He has accused her of shameful conduct, saying, “I discovered that your daughter was not a virgin.” But here is the proof of my daughter’s virginity.’ Then they must spread her bed sheet before the elders.
22.18: The elders must then take the man and punish him.
22.19: They must also fine him 100 pieces of silver, which he must pay to the woman’s father because he publicly accused a virgin of Israel of shameful conduct. The woman will then remain the man’s wife, and he may never divorce her.
22.20: “But suppose the man’s accusations are true, and he can show that she was not a virgin.
22.21: The woman must be taken to the door of her father’s home, and there the men of the town must stone her to death, for she has committed a disgraceful crime in Israel by being promiscuous while living in her parents’ home. In this way, you will purge this evil from among you.
22.22: “If a man is discovered committing adultery, both he and the woman must die. In this way, you will purge Israel of such evil.
22.23: “Suppose a man meets a young woman, a virgin who is engaged to be married, and he has sexual intercourse with her. If this happens within a town,
22.24: you must take both of them to the gates of that town and stone them to death. The woman is guilty because she did not scream for help. The man must die because he violated another man’s wife. In this way, you will purge this evil from among you.
22.25: “But if the man meets the engaged woman out in the country, and he rapes her, then only the man must die.
22.26: Do nothing to the young woman; she has committed no crime worthy of death. She is as innocent as a murder victim.
22.27: Since the man raped her out in the country, it must be assumed that she screamed, but there was no one to rescue her.
22.28: “Suppose a man has intercourse with a young woman who is a virgin but is not engaged to be married. If they are discovered,
22.29: he must pay her father fifty pieces of silver. Then he must marry the young woman because he violated her, and he may never divorce her as long as he lives.
22.30: “A man must not marry his father’s former wife, for this would violate his father.

29.1: These are the terms of the covenant the Lord commanded Moses to make with the Israelites while they were in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he had made with them at Mount Sinai.
29.2: Moses summoned all the Israelites and said to them, “You have seen with your own eyes everything the Lord did in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to his whole country—
29.3: all the great tests of strength, the miraculous signs, and the amazing wonders.
29.4: But to this day the Lord has not given you minds that understand, nor eyes that see, nor ears that hear!
29.5: For forty years I led you through the wilderness, yet your clothes and sandals did not wear out.
29.6: You ate no bread and drank no wine or other alcoholic drink, but he provided for you so you would know that he is the Lord your God.
29.7: “When we came here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan came out to fight against us, but we defeated them.
29.8: We took their land and gave it to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and to the half-tribe of Manasseh as their grant of land.
29.9: “Therefore, obey the terms of this covenant so that you will prosper in everything you do.
29.10: All of you—tribal leaders, elders, officers, all the men of Israel—are standing today in the presence of the Lord your God.
29.11: Your little ones and your wives are with you, as well as the foreigners living among you who chop your wood and carry your water.
29.12: You are standing here today to enter into the covenant of the Lord your God. The Lord is making this covenant, including the curses.
29.13: By entering into the covenant today, he will establish you as his people and confirm that he is your God, just as he promised you and as he swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
29.14: “But you are not the only ones with whom I am making this covenant with its curses.
29.15: I am making this covenant both with you who stand here today in the presence of the Lord our God, and also with the future generations who are not standing here today.
29.16: “You remember how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we traveled through the lands of enemy nations as we left.
29.17: You have seen their detestable practices and their idols made of wood, stone, silver, and gold.
29.18: I am making this covenant with you so that no one among you—no man, woman, clan, or tribe—will turn away from the Lord our God to worship these gods of other nations, and so that no root among you bears bitter and poisonous fruit.
29.19: “Those who hear the warnings of this curse should not congratulate themselves, thinking, ‘I am safe, even though I am following the desires of my own stubborn heart.’ This would lead to utter ruin!
29.20: The Lord will never pardon such people. Instead his anger and jealousy will burn against them. All the curses written in this book will come down on them, and the Lord will erase their names from under heaven.
29.21: The Lord will separate them from all the tribes of Israel, to pour out on them all the curses of the covenant recorded in this Book of Instruction.
29.22: “Then the generations to come, both your own descendants and the foreigners who come from distant lands, will see the devastation of the land and the diseases the Lord inflicts on it.
29.23: They will exclaim, ‘The whole land is devastated by sulfur and salt. It is a wasteland with nothing planted and nothing growing, not even a blade of grass. It is like the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord destroyed in his intense anger.’
29.24: “And all the surrounding nations will ask, ‘Why has the Lord done this to this land? Why was he so angry?’
29.25: “And the answer will be, ‘This happened because the people of the land abandoned the covenant that the Lord, the God of their ancestors, made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
29.26: Instead, they turned away to serve and worship gods they had not known before, gods that were not from the Lord.
29.27: That is why the Lord’s anger has burned against this land, bringing down on it every curse recorded in this book.
29.28: In great anger and fury the Lord uprooted his people from their land and banished them to another land, where they still live today!’
29.29: “The Lord our God has secrets known to no one. We are not accountable for them, but we and our children are accountable forever for all that he has revealed to us, so that we may obey all the terms of these instructions.

3.1: “Next we turned and headed for the land of Bashan, where King Og and his entire army attacked us at Edrei.
3.2: But the Lord told me, ‘Do not be afraid of him, for I have given you victory over Og and his entire army, and I will give you all his land. Treat him just as you treated King Sihon of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon.’
3.3: “So the Lord our God handed King Og and all his people over to us, and we killed them all. Not a single person survived.
3.4: We conquered all sixty of his towns—the entire Argob region in his kingdom of Bashan. Not a single town escaped our conquest.
3.5: These towns were all fortified with high walls and barred gates. We also took many unwalled villages at the same time.
3.6: We completely destroyed the kingdom of Bashan, just as we had destroyed King Sihon of Heshbon. We destroyed all the people in every town we conquered—men, women, and children alike.
3.7: But we kept all the livestock for ourselves and took plunder from all the towns.
3.8: “So we took the land of the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River—all the way from the Arnon Gorge to Mount Hermon.
3.9: (Mount Hermon is called Sirion by the Sidonians, and the Amorites call it Senir.)
3.10: We had now conquered all the cities on the plateau and all Gilead and Bashan, as far as the towns of Salecah and Edrei, which were part of Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
3.11: (King Og of Bashan was the last survivor of the giant Rephaites. His bed was made of iron and was more than thirteen feet long and six feet wide. It can still be seen in the Ammonite city of Rabbah.)
3.12: “When we took possession of this land, I gave to the tribes of Reuben and Gad the territory beyond Aroer along the Arnon Gorge, plus half of the hill country of Gilead with its towns.
3.13: Then I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan—Og’s former kingdom—to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (This entire Argob region of Bashan used to be known as the land of the Rephaites.
3.14: Jair, a leader from the tribe of Manasseh, conquered the whole Argob region in Bashan, all the way to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. Jair renamed this region after himself, calling it the Towns of Jair, as it is still known today.)
3.15: I gave Gilead to the clan of Makir.
3.16: But I also gave part of Gilead to the tribes of Reuben and Gad. The area I gave them extended from the middle of the Arnon Gorge in the south to the Jabbok River on the Ammonite frontier.
3.17: They also received the Jordan Valley, all the way from the Sea of Galilee down to the Dead Sea, with the Jordan River serving as the western boundary. To the east were the slopes of Pisgah.
3.18: “At that time I gave this command to the tribes that would live east of the Jordan: ‘Although the Lord your God has given you this land as your property, all your fighting men must cross the Jordan ahead of your Israelite relatives, armed and ready to assist them.
3.19: Your wives, children, and numerous livestock, however, may stay behind in the towns I have given you.
3.20: When the Lord has given security to the rest of the Israelites, as he has to you, and when they occupy the land the Lord your God is giving them across the Jordan River, then you may all return here to the land I have given you.’
3.21: “At that time I gave Joshua this charge: ‘You have seen for yourself everything the Lord your God has done to these two kings. He will do the same to all the kingdoms on the west side of the Jordan.
3.22: Do not be afraid of the nations there, for the Lord your God will fight for you.’
3.23: “At that time I pleaded with the Lord and said,
3.24: ‘O Sovereign Lord, you have only begun to show your greatness and the strength of your hand to me, your servant. Is there any god in heaven or on earth who can perform such great and mighty deeds as you do?
3.25: Please let me cross the Jordan to see the wonderful land on the other side, the beautiful hill country and the Lebanon mountains.’
3.26: “But the Lord was angry with me because of you, and he would not listen to me. ‘That’s enough!’ he declared. ‘Speak of it no more.
3.27: But go up to Pisgah Peak, and look over the land in every direction. Take a good look, but you may not cross the Jordan River.
3.28: Instead, commission Joshua and encourage and strengthen him, for he will lead the people across the Jordan. He will give them all the land you now see before you as their possession.’
3.29: So we stayed in the valley near Beth-peor.

13.1: “Suppose there are prophets among you or those who dream dreams about the future, and they promise you signs or miracles,
13.2: and the predicted signs or miracles occur. If they then say, ‘Come, let us worship other gods’—gods you have not known before—
13.3: do not listen to them. The Lord your God is testing you to see if you truly love him with all your heart and soul.
13.4: Serve only the Lord your God and fear him alone. Obey his commands, listen to his voice, and cling to him.
13.5: The false prophets or visionaries who try to lead you astray must be put to death, for they encourage rebellion against the Lord your God, who redeemed you from slavery and brought you out of the land of Egypt. Since they try to lead you astray from the way the Lord your God commanded you to live, you must put them to death. In this way you will purge the evil from among you.
13.6: “Suppose someone secretly entices you—even your brother, your son or daughter, your beloved wife, or your closest friend—and says, ‘Let us go worship other gods’—gods that neither you nor your ancestors have known.
13.7: They might suggest that you worship the gods of peoples who live nearby or who come from the ends of the earth.
13.8: But do not give in or listen. Have no pity, and do not spare or protect them.
13.9: You must put them to death! Strike the first blow yourself, and then all the people must join in.
13.10: Stone the guilty ones to death because they have tried to draw you away from the Lord your God, who rescued you from the land of Egypt, the place of slavery.
13.11: Then all Israel will hear about it and be afraid, and no one will act so wickedly again.
13.12: “When you begin living in the towns the Lord your God is giving you, you may hear
13.13: that scoundrels among you are leading their fellow citizens astray by saying, ‘Let us go worship other gods’—gods you have not known before.
13.14: In such cases, you must examine the facts carefully. If you find that the report is true and such a detestable act has been committed among you,
13.15: you must attack that town and completely destroy all its inhabitants, as well as all the livestock.
13.16: Then you must pile all the plunder in the middle of the open square and burn it. Burn the entire town as a burnt offering to the Lord your God. That town must remain a ruin forever; it may never be rebuilt.
13.17: Keep none of the plunder that has been set apart for destruction. Then the Lord will turn from his fierce anger and be merciful to you. He will have compassion on you and make you a large nation, just as he swore to your ancestors.
13.18: “The Lord your God will be merciful only if you listen to his voice and keep all his commands that I am giving you today, doing what pleases him.

25.1: “Suppose two people take a dispute to court, and the judges declare that one is right and the other is wrong.
25.2: If the person in the wrong is sentenced to be flogged, the judge must command him to lie down and be beaten in his presence with the number of lashes appropriate to the crime.
25.3: But never give more than forty lashes; more than forty lashes would publicly humiliate your neighbor.
25.4: “You must not muzzle an ox to keep it from eating as it treads out the grain.
25.5: “If two brothers are living together on the same property and one of them dies without a son, his widow may not be married to anyone from outside the family. Instead, her husband’s brother should marry her and have intercourse with her to fulfill the duties of a brother-in-law.
25.6: The first son she bears to him will be considered the son of the dead brother, so that his name will not be forgotten in Israel.
25.7: “But if the man refuses to marry his brother’s widow, she must go to the town gate and say to the elders assembled there, ‘My husband’s brother refuses to preserve his brother’s name in Israel—he refuses to fulfill the duties of a brother-in-law by marrying me.’
25.8: The elders of the town will then summon him and talk with him. If he still refuses and says, ‘I don’t want to marry her,’
25.9: the widow must walk over to him in the presence of the elders, pull his sandal from his foot, and spit in his face. Then she must declare, ‘This is what happens to a man who refuses to provide his brother with children.’
25.10: Ever afterward in Israel his family will be referred to as ‘the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off’!
25.11: “If two Israelite men get into a fight and the wife of one tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the testicles of the other man,
25.12: you must cut off her hand. Show her no pity.
25.13: “You must use accurate scales when you weigh out merchandise,
25.14: and you must use full and honest measures.
25.15: Yes, always use honest weights and measures, so that you may enjoy a long life in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
25.16: All who cheat with dishonest weights and measures are detestable to the Lord your God.
25.17: “Never forget what the Amalekites did to you as you came from Egypt.
25.18: They attacked you when you were exhausted and weary, and they struck down those who were straggling behind. They had no fear of God.
25.19: Therefore, when the Lord your God has given you rest from all your enemies in the land he is giving you as a special possession, you must destroy the Amalekites and erase their memory from under heaven. Never forget this!

33.1: This is the blessing that Moses, the man of God, gave to the people of Israel before his death:
33.2: “The Lord came from Mount Sinai and dawned upon us from Mount Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran and came from Meribah-kadesh with flaming fire at his right hand.
33.3: Indeed, he loves his people; all his holy ones are in his hands. They follow in his steps and accept his teaching.
33.4: Moses gave us the Lord’s instruction, the special possession of the people of Israel.
33.5: The Lord became king in Israel— when the leaders of the people assembled, when the tribes of Israel gathered as one.”
33.6: Moses said this about the tribe of Reuben: “Let the tribe of Reuben live and not die out, though they are few in number.”
33.7: Moses said this about the tribe of Judah: “O Lord, hear the cry of Judah and bring them together as a people. Give them strength to defend their cause; help them against their enemies!”
33.8: Moses said this about the tribe of Levi: “O Lord, you have given your Thummim and Urim—the sacred lots— to your faithful servants the Levites. You put them to the test at Massah and struggled with them at the waters of Meribah.
33.9: The Levites obeyed your word and guarded your covenant. They were more loyal to you than to their own parents. They ignored their relatives and did not acknowledge their own children.
33.10: They teach your regulations to Jacob; they give your instructions to Israel. They present incense before you and offer whole burnt offerings on the altar.
33.11: Bless the ministry of the Levites, O Lord, and accept all the work of their hands. Hit their enemies where it hurts the most; strike down their foes so they never rise again.”
33.12: Moses said this about the tribe of Benjamin: “The people of Benjamin are loved by the Lord and live in safety beside him. He surrounds them continuously and preserves them from every harm.”
33.13: Moses said this about the tribes of Joseph: “May their land be blessed by the Lord with the precious gift of dew from the heavens and water from beneath the earth
33.14: with the rich fruit that grows in the sun, and the rich harvest produced each month
33.15: with the finest crops of the ancient mountains, and the abundance from the everlasting hills
33.16: with the best gifts of the earth and its bounty, and the favor of the one who appeared in the burning bush. May these blessings rest on Joseph’s head, crowning the brow of the prince among his brothers.
33.17: Joseph has the majesty of a young bull; he has the horns of a wild ox. He will gore distant nations, even to the ends of the earth. This is my blessing for the multitudes of Ephraim and the thousands of Manasseh.”
33.18: Moses said this about the tribes of Zebulun and Issachar: “May the people of Zebulun prosper in their travels. May the people of Issachar prosper at home in their tents.
33.19: They summon the people to the mountain to offer proper sacrifices there. They benefit from the riches of the sea and the hidden treasures in the sand.”
33.20: Moses said this about the tribe of Gad: “Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad’s territory! Gad is poised there like a lion to tear off an arm or a head.
33.21: The people of Gad took the best land for themselves; a leader’s share was assigned to them. When the leaders of the people were assembled, they carried out the Lord’s justice and obeyed his regulations for Israel.”
33.22: Moses said this about the tribe of Dan: “Dan is a lion’s cub, leaping out from Bashan.”
33.23: Moses said this about the tribe of Naphtali: “O Naphtali, you are rich in favor and full of the Lord’s blessings; may you possess the west and the south.”
33.24: Moses said this about the tribe of Asher: “May Asher be blessed above other sons; may he be esteemed by his brothers; may he bathe his feet in olive oil.
33.25: May the bolts of your gates be of iron and bronze; may you be secure all your days.”
33.26: “There is no one like the God of Israel. He rides across the heavens to help you, across the skies in majestic splendor.
33.27: The eternal God is your refuge, and his everlasting arms are under you. He drives out the enemy before you; he cries out, ‘Destroy them!’
33.28: So Israel will live in safety, prosperous Jacob in security, in a land of grain and new wine, while the heavens drop down dew.
33.29: How blessed you are, O Israel! Who else is like you, a people saved by the Lord? He is your protecting shield and your triumphant sword! Your enemies will cringe before you, and you will stomp on their backs!”

32.1: “Listen, O heavens, and I will speak! Hear, O earth, the words that I say!
32.2: Let my teaching fall on you like rain; let my speech settle like dew. Let my words fall like rain on tender grass, like gentle showers on young plants.
32.3: I will proclaim the name of the Lord; how glorious is our God!
32.4: He is the Rock; his deeds are perfect. Everything he does is just and fair. He is a faithful God who does no wrong; how just and upright he is!
32.5: “But they have acted corruptly toward him; when they act so perversely, are they really his children? They are a deceitful and twisted generation.
32.6: Is this the way you repay the Lord, you foolish and senseless people? Isn’t he your Father who created you? Has he not made you and established you?
32.7: Remember the days of long ago; think about the generations past. Ask your father, and he will inform you. Inquire of your elders, and they will tell you.
32.8: When the Most High assigned lands to the nations, when he divided up the human race, he established the boundaries of the peoples according to the number in his heavenly court.
32.9: “For the people of Israel belong to the Lord; Jacob is his special possession.
32.10: He found them in a desert land, in an empty, howling wasteland. He surrounded them and watched over them; he guarded them as he would guard his own eyes.
32.11: Like an eagle that rouses her chicks and hovers over her young, so he spread his wings to take them up and carried them safely on his pinions.
32.12: The Lord alone guided them; they followed no foreign gods.
32.13: He let them ride over the highlands and feast on the crops of the fields. He nourished them with honey from the rock and olive oil from the stony ground.
32.14: He fed them yogurt from the herd and milk from the flock, together with the fat of lambs. He gave them choice rams from Bashan, and goats, together with the choicest wheat. You drank the finest wine, made from the juice of grapes.
32.15: “But Israel soon became fat and unruly; the people grew heavy, plump, and stuffed! Then they abandoned the God who had made them; they made light of the Rock of their salvation.
32.16: They stirred up his jealousy by worshiping foreign gods; they provoked his fury with detestable deeds.
32.17: They offered sacrifices to demons, which are not God, to gods they had not known before, to new gods only recently arrived, to gods their ancestors had never feared.
32.18: You neglected the Rock who had fathered you; you forgot the God who had given you birth.
32.19: “The Lord saw this and drew back, provoked to anger by his own sons and daughters.
32.20: He said, ‘I will abandon them; then see what becomes of them. For they are a twisted generation, children without integrity.
32.21: They have roused my jealousy by worshiping things that are not God; they have provoked my anger with their useless idols. Now I will rouse their jealousy through people who are not even a people; I will provoke their anger through the foolish Gentiles.
32.22: For my anger blazes forth like fire and burns to the depths of the grave. It devours the earth and all its crops and ignites the foundations of the mountains.
32.23: I will heap disasters upon them and shoot them down with my arrows.
32.24: I will weaken them with famine, burning fever, and deadly disease. I will send the fangs of wild beasts and poisonous snakes that glide in the dust.
32.25: Outside, the sword will bring death, and inside, terror will strike both young men and young women, both infants and the aged.
32.26: I would have annihilated them, wiping out even the memory of them.
32.27: But I feared the taunt of Israel’s enemy, who might misunderstand and say, “Our own power has triumphed! The Lord had nothing to do with this!”’
32.28: “But Israel is a senseless nation; the people are foolish, without understanding.
32.29: Oh, that they were wise and could understand this! Oh, that they might know their fate!
32.30: How could one person chase a thousand of them, and two people put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, unless the Lord had given them up?
32.31: But the rock of our enemies is not like our Rock, as even they recognize.
32.32: Their vine grows from the vine of Sodom, from the vineyards of Gomorrah. Their grapes are poison, and their clusters are bitter.
32.33: Their wine is the venom of serpents, the deadly poison of cobras.
32.34: “The Lord says, ‘Am I not storing up these things, sealing them away in my treasury?
32.35: I will take revenge; I will pay them back. In due time their feet will slip. Their day of disaster will arrive, and their destiny will overtake them.’
32.36: “Indeed, the Lord will give justice to his people, and he will change his mind about his servants, when he sees their strength is gone and no one is left, slave or free.
32.37: Then he will ask, ‘Where are their gods, the rocks they fled to for refuge?
32.38: Where now are those gods, who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their offerings? Let those gods arise and help you! Let them provide you with shelter!
32.39: Look now; I myself am he! There is no other god but me! I am the one who kills and gives life; I am the one who wounds and heals; no one can be rescued from my powerful hand!
32.40: Now I raise my hand to heaven and declare, “As surely as I live,
32.41: when I sharpen my flashing sword and begin to carry out justice, I will take revenge on my enemies and repay those who reject me.
32.42: I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh— the blood of the slaughtered and the captives, and the heads of the enemy leaders.”’
32.43: “Rejoice with him, you heavens, and let all of God’s angels worship him. Rejoice with his people, you Gentiles, and let all the angels be strengthened in him. For he will avenge the blood of his children; he will take revenge against his enemies. He will repay those who hate him and cleanse his people’s land.”
32.44: So Moses came with Joshua son of Nun and recited all the words of this song to the people.
32.45: When Moses had finished reciting all these words to the people of Israel,
32.46: he added: “Take to heart all the words of warning I have given you today. Pass them on as a command to your children so they will obey every word of these instructions.
32.47: These instructions are not empty words—they are your life! By obeying them you will enjoy a long life in the land you will occupy when you cross the Jordan River.”
32.48: That same day the Lord said to Moses,
32.49: “Go to Moab, to the mountains east of the river, and climb Mount Nebo, which is across from Jericho. Look out across the land of Canaan, the land I am giving to the people of Israel as their own special possession.
32.50: Then you will die there on the mountain. You will join your ancestors, just as Aaron, your brother, died on Mount Hor and joined his ancestors.
32.51: For both of you betrayed me with the Israelites at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin. You failed to demonstrate my holiness to the people of Israel there.
32.52: So you will see the land from a distance, but you may not enter the land I am giving to the people of Israel.”

24.1: “Suppose a man marries a woman but she does not please him. Having discovered something wrong with her, he writes a document of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house.
24.2: When she leaves his house, she is free to marry another man.
24.3: But if the second husband also turns against her, writes a document of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away, or if he dies,
24.4: the first husband may not marry her again, for she has been defiled. That would be detestable to the Lord. You must not bring guilt upon the land the Lord your God is giving you as a special possession.
24.5: “A newly married man must not be drafted into the army or be given any other official responsibilities. He must be free to spend one year at home, bringing happiness to the wife he has married.
24.6: “It is wrong to take a set of millstones, or even just the upper millstone, as security for a loan, for the owner uses it to make a living.
24.7: “If anyone kidnaps a fellow Israelite and treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. In this way, you will purge the evil from among you.
24.8: “In all cases involving serious skin diseases, be careful to follow the instructions of the Levitical priests; obey all the commands I have given them.
24.9: Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam as you were coming from Egypt.
24.10: “If you lend anything to your neighbor, do not enter his house to pick up the item he is giving as security.
24.11: You must wait outside while he goes in and brings it out to you.
24.12: If your neighbor is poor and gives you his cloak as security for a loan, do not keep the cloak overnight.
24.13: Return the cloak to its owner by sunset so he can stay warm through the night and bless you, and the Lord your God will count you as righteous.
24.14: “Never take advantage of poor and destitute laborers, whether they are fellow Israelites or foreigners living in your towns.
24.15: You must pay them their wages each day before sunset because they are poor and are counting on it. If you don’t, they might cry out to the Lord against you, and it would be counted against you as sin.
24.16: “Parents must not be put to death for the sins of their children, nor children for the sins of their parents. Those deserving to die must be put to death for their own crimes.
24.17: “True justice must be given to foreigners living among you and to orphans, and you must never accept a widow’s garment as security for her debt.
24.18: Always remember that you were slaves in Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you from your slavery. That is why I have given you this command.
24.19: “When you are harvesting your crops and forget to bring in a bundle of grain from your field, don’t go back to get it. Leave it for the foreigners, orphans, and widows. Then the Lord your God will bless you in all you do.
24.20: When you beat the olives from your olive trees, don’t go over the boughs twice. Leave the remaining olives for the foreigners, orphans, and widows.
24.21: When you gather the grapes in your vineyard, don’t glean the vines after they are picked. Leave the remaining grapes for the foreigners, orphans, and widows.
24.22: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That is why I am giving you this command.

12.1: “These are the decrees and regulations you must be careful to obey when you live in the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, is giving you. You must obey them as long as you live.
12.2: “When you drive out the nations that live there, you must destroy all the places where they worship their gods—high on the mountains, up on the hills, and under every green tree.
12.3: Break down their altars and smash their sacred pillars. Burn their Asherah poles and cut down their carved idols. Completely erase the names of their gods!
12.4: “Do not worship the Lord your God in the way these pagan peoples worship their gods.
12.5: Rather, you must seek the Lord your God at the place of worship he himself will choose from among all the tribes—the place where his name will be honored.
12.6: There you will bring your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, your sacred offerings, your offerings to fulfill a vow, your voluntary offerings, and your offerings of the firstborn animals of your herds and flocks.
12.7: There you and your families will feast in the presence of the Lord your God, and you will rejoice in all you have accomplished because the Lord your God has blessed you.
12.8: “Your pattern of worship will change. Today all of you are doing as you please,
12.9: because you have not yet arrived at the place of rest, the land the Lord your God is giving you as your special possession.
12.10: But you will soon cross the Jordan River and live in the land the Lord your God is giving you. When he gives you rest from all your enemies and you’re living safely in the land,
12.11: you must bring everything I command you—your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, your sacred offerings, and your offerings to fulfill a vow—to the designated place of worship, the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to be honored.
12.12: “You must celebrate there in the presence of the Lord your God with your sons and daughters and all your servants. And remember to include the Levites who live in your towns, for they will receive no allotment of land among you.
12.13: Be careful not to sacrifice your burnt offerings just anywhere you like.
12.14: You may do so only at the place the Lord will choose within one of your tribal territories. There you must offer your burnt offerings and do everything I command you.
12.15: “But you may butcher your animals and eat their meat in any town whenever you want. You may freely eat the animals with which the Lord your God blesses you. All of you, whether ceremonially clean or unclean, may eat that meat, just as you now eat gazelle and deer.
12.16: But you must not consume the blood. You must pour it out on the ground like water.
12.17: “But you may not eat your offerings in your hometown—neither the tithe of your grain and new wine and olive oil, nor the firstborn of your flocks and herds, nor any offering to fulfill a vow, nor your voluntary offerings, nor your sacred offerings.
12.18: You must eat these in the presence of the Lord your God at the place he will choose. Eat them there with your children, your servants, and the Levites who live in your towns, celebrating in the presence of the Lord your God in all you do.
12.19: And be very careful never to neglect the Levites as long as you live in your land.
12.20: “When the Lord your God expands your territory as he has promised, and you have the urge to eat meat, you may freely eat meat whenever you want.
12.21: It might happen that the designated place of worship—the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to be honored—is a long way from your home. If so, you may butcher any of the cattle, sheep, or goats the Lord has given you, and you may freely eat the meat in your hometown, as I have commanded you.
12.22: Anyone, whether ceremonially clean or unclean, may eat that meat, just as you do now with gazelle and deer.
12.23: But never consume the blood, for the blood is the life, and you must not consume the lifeblood with the meat.
12.24: Instead, pour out the blood on the ground like water.
12.25: Do not consume the blood, so that all may go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what pleases the Lord.
12.26: “Take your sacred gifts and your offerings given to fulfill a vow to the place the Lord chooses.
12.27: You must offer the meat and blood of your burnt offerings on the altar of the Lord your God. The blood of your other sacrifices must be poured out on the altar of the Lord your God, but you may eat the meat.
12.28: Be careful to obey all my commands, so that all will go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is good and pleasing to the Lord your God.
12.29: “When the Lord your God goes ahead of you and destroys the nations and you drive them out and live in their land,
12.30: do not fall into the trap of following their customs and worshiping their gods. Do not inquire about their gods, saying, ‘How do these nations worship their gods? I want to follow their example.’
12.31: You must not worship the Lord your God the way the other nations worship their gods, for they perform for their gods every detestable act that the Lord hates. They even burn their sons and daughters as sacrifices to their gods.
12.32: “So be careful to obey all the commands I give you. You must not add anything to them or subtract anything from them.

2.1: “Then we turned around and headed back across the wilderness toward the Red Sea, just as the Lord had instructed me, and we wandered around in the region of Mount Seir for a long time.
2.2: “Then at last the Lord said to me,
2.3: ‘You have been wandering around in this hill country long enough; turn to the north.
2.4: Give these orders to the people: “You will pass through the country belonging to your relatives the Edomites, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. The Edomites will feel threatened, so be careful.
2.5: Do not bother them, for I have given them all the hill country around Mount Seir as their property, and I will not give you even one square foot of their land.
2.6: If you need food to eat or water to drink, pay them for it.
2.7: For the Lord your God has blessed you in everything you have done. He has watched your every step through this great wilderness. During these forty years, the Lord your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing.”’
2.8: “So we bypassed the territory of our relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. We avoided the road through the Arabah Valley that comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber. “Then as we turned north along the desert route through Moab,
2.9: the Lord warned us, ‘Do not bother the Moabites, the descendants of Lot, or start a war with them. I have given them Ar as their property, and I will not give you any of their land.’”
2.10: (A race of giants called the Emites had once lived in the area of Ar. They were as strong and numerous and tall as the Anakites, another race of giants.
2.11: Both the Emites and the Anakites are also known as the Rephaites, though the Moabites call them Emites.
2.12: In earlier times the Horites had lived in Seir, but they were driven out and displaced by the descendants of Esau, just as Israel drove out the people of Canaan when the Lord gave Israel their land.)
2.13: Moses continued, “Then the Lord said to us, ‘Get moving. Cross the Zered Brook.’ So we crossed the brook.
2.14: “Thirty-eight years passed from the time we first left Kadesh-barnea until we finally crossed the Zered Brook! By then, all the men old enough to fight in battle had died in the wilderness, as the Lord had vowed would happen.
2.15: The Lord struck them down until they had all been eliminated from the community.
2.16: “When all the men of fighting age had died,
2.18: ‘Today you will cross the border of Moab at Ar
2.19: and enter the land of the Ammonites, the descendants of Lot. But do not bother them or start a war with them. I have given the land of Ammon to them as their property, and I will not give you any of their land.’”
2.20: (That area was once considered the land of the Rephaites, who had lived there, though the Ammonites call them Zamzummites.
2.21: They were also as strong and numerous and tall as the Anakites. But the Lord destroyed them so the Ammonites could occupy their land.
2.22: He had done the same for the descendants of Esau who lived in Seir, for he destroyed the Horites so they could settle there in their place. The descendants of Esau live there to this day.
2.23: A similar thing happened when the Caphtorites from Crete invaded and destroyed the Avvites, who had lived in villages in the area of Gaza.)
2.24: Moses continued, “Then the Lord said, ‘Now get moving! Cross the Arnon Gorge. Look, I will hand over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and I will give you his land. Attack him and begin to occupy the land.
2.25: Beginning today I will make people throughout the earth terrified because of you. When they hear reports about you, they will tremble with dread and fear.’”
2.26: Moses continued, “From the wilderness of Kedemoth I sent ambassadors to King Sihon of Heshbon with this proposal of peace:
2.27: ‘Let us travel through your land. We will stay on the main road and won’t turn off into the fields on either side.
2.28: Sell us food to eat and water to drink, and we will pay for it. All we want is permission to pass through your land.
2.29: The descendants of Esau who live in Seir allowed us to go through their country, and so did the Moabites, who live in Ar. Let us pass through until we cross the Jordan into the land the Lord our God is giving us.’
2.30: “But King Sihon of Heshbon refused to allow us to pass through, because the Lord your God made Sihon stubborn and defiant so he could help you defeat him, as he has now done.
2.31: “Then the Lord said to me, ‘Look, I have begun to hand King Sihon and his land over to you. Begin now to conquer and occupy his land.’
2.32: “Then King Sihon declared war on us and mobilized his forces at Jahaz.
2.33: But the Lord our God handed him over to us, and we crushed him, his sons, and all his people.
2.34: We conquered all his towns and completely destroyed everyone—men, women, and children. Not a single person was spared.
2.35: We took all the livestock as plunder for ourselves, along with anything of value from the towns we ransacked.
2.36: “The Lord our God also helped us conquer Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Gorge, and the town in the gorge, and the whole area as far as Gilead. No town had walls too strong for us.
2.37: However, we avoided the land of the Ammonites all along the Jabbok River and the towns in the hill country—all the places the Lord our God had commanded us to leave alone.

28.1: “If you fully obey the Lord your God and carefully keep all his commands that I am giving you today, the Lord your God will set you high above all the nations of the world.
28.2: You will experience all these blessings if you obey the Lord your God:
28.3: Your towns and your fields will be blessed.
28.4: Your children and your crops will be blessed. The offspring of your herds and flocks will be blessed.
28.5: Your fruit baskets and breadboards will be blessed.
28.6: Wherever you go and whatever you do, you will be blessed.
28.7: “The Lord will conquer your enemies when they attack you. They will attack you from one direction, but they will scatter from you in seven!
28.8: “The Lord will guarantee a blessing on everything you do and will fill your storehouses with grain. The Lord your God will bless you in the land he is giving you.
28.9: “If you obey the commands of the Lord your God and walk in his ways, the Lord will establish you as his holy people as he swore he would do.
28.10: Then all the nations of the world will see that you are a people claimed by the Lord, and they will stand in awe of you.
28.11: “The Lord will give you prosperity in the land he swore to your ancestors to give you, blessing you with many children, numerous livestock, and abundant crops.
28.12: The Lord will send rain at the proper time from his rich treasury in the heavens and will bless all the work you do. You will lend to many nations, but you will never need to borrow from them.
28.13: If you listen to these commands of the Lord your God that I am giving you today, and if you carefully obey them, the Lord will make you the head and not the tail, and you will always be on top and never at the bottom.
28.14: You must not turn away from any of the commands I am giving you today, nor follow after other gods and worship them.
28.15: “But if you refuse to listen to the Lord your God and do not obey all the commands and decrees I am giving you today, all these curses will come and overwhelm you:
28.16: Your towns and your fields will be cursed.
28.17: Your fruit baskets and breadboards will be cursed.
28.18: Your children and your crops will be cursed. The offspring of your herds and flocks will be cursed.
28.19: Wherever you go and whatever you do, you will be cursed.
28.20: “The Lord himself will send on you curses, confusion, and frustration in everything you do, until at last you are completely destroyed for doing evil and abandoning me.
28.21: The Lord will afflict you with diseases until none of you are left in the land you are about to enter and occupy.
28.22: The Lord will strike you with wasting diseases, fever, and inflammation, with scorching heat and drought, and with blight and mildew. These disasters will pursue you until you die.
28.23: The skies above will be as unyielding as bronze, and the earth beneath will be as hard as iron.
28.24: The Lord will change the rain that falls on your land into powder, and dust will pour down from the sky until you are destroyed.
28.25: “The Lord will cause you to be defeated by your enemies. You will attack your enemies from one direction, but you will scatter from them in seven! You will be an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
28.26: Your corpses will be food for all the scavenging birds and wild animals, and no one will be there to chase them away.
28.27: “The Lord will afflict you with the boils of Egypt and with tumors, scurvy, and the itch, from which you cannot be cured.
28.28: The Lord will strike you with madness, blindness, and panic.
28.29: You will grope around in broad daylight like a blind person groping in the darkness, but you will not find your way. You will be oppressed and robbed continually, and no one will come to save you.
28.30: “You will be engaged to a woman, but another man will sleep with her. You will build a house, but someone else will live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will never enjoy its fruit.
28.31: Your ox will be butchered before your eyes, but you will not eat a single bite of the meat. Your donkey will be taken from you, never to be returned. Your sheep and goats will be given to your enemies, and no one will be there to help you.
28.32: You will watch as your sons and daughters are taken away as slaves. Your heart will break for them, but you won’t be able to help them.
28.33: A foreign nation you have never heard about will eat the crops you worked so hard to grow. You will suffer under constant oppression and harsh treatment.
28.34: You will go mad because of all the tragedy you see around you.
28.35: The Lord will cover your knees and legs with incurable boils. In fact, you will be covered from head to foot.
28.36: “The Lord will exile you and your king to a nation unknown to you and your ancestors. There in exile you will worship gods of wood and stone!
28.37: You will become an object of horror, ridicule, and mockery among all the nations to which the Lord sends you.
28.38: “You will plant much but harvest little, for locusts will eat your crops.
28.39: You will plant vineyards and care for them, but you will not drink the wine or eat the grapes, for worms will destroy the vines.
28.40: You will grow olive trees throughout your land, but you will never use the olive oil, for the fruit will drop before it ripens.
28.41: You will have sons and daughters, but you will lose them, for they will be led away into captivity.
28.42: Swarms of insects will destroy your trees and crops.
28.43: “The foreigners living among you will become stronger and stronger, while you become weaker and weaker.
28.44: They will lend money to you, but you will not lend to them. They will be the head, and you will be the tail!
28.45: “If you refuse to listen to the Lord your God and to obey the commands and decrees he has given you, all these curses will pursue and overtake you until you are destroyed.
28.46: These horrors will serve as a sign and warning among you and your descendants forever.
28.47: If you do not serve the Lord your God with joy and enthusiasm for the abundant benefits you have received,
28.48: you will serve your enemies whom the Lord will send against you. You will be left hungry, thirsty, naked, and lacking in everything. The Lord will put an iron yoke on your neck, oppressing you harshly until he has destroyed you.
28.49: “The Lord will bring a distant nation against you from the end of the earth, and it will swoop down on you like a vulture. It is a nation whose language you do not understand,
28.50: a fierce and heartless nation that shows no respect for the old and no pity for the young.
28.51: Its armies will devour your livestock and crops, and you will be destroyed. They will leave you no grain, new wine, olive oil, calves, or lambs, and you will starve to death.
28.52: They will attack your cities until all the fortified walls in your land—the walls you trusted to protect you—are knocked down. They will attack all the towns in the land the Lord your God has given you.
28.53: “The siege and terrible distress of the enemy’s attack will be so severe that you will eat the flesh of your own sons and daughters, whom the Lord your God has given you.
28.54: The most tenderhearted man among you will have no compassion for his own brother, his beloved wife, and his surviving children.
28.55: He will refuse to share with them the flesh he is devouring—the flesh of one of his own children—because he has nothing else to eat during the siege and terrible distress that your enemy will inflict on all your towns.
28.56: The most tender and delicate woman among you—so delicate she would not so much as touch the ground with her foot—will be selfish toward the husband she loves and toward her own son or daughter.
28.57: She will hide from them the afterbirth and the new baby she has borne, so that she herself can secretly eat them. She will have nothing else to eat during the siege and terrible distress that your enemy will inflict on all your towns.
28.58: “If you refuse to obey all the words of instruction that are written in this book, and if you do not fear the glorious and awesome name of the Lord your God,
28.59: then the Lord will overwhelm you and your children with indescribable plagues. These plagues will be intense and without relief, making you miserable and unbearably sick.
28.60: He will afflict you with all the diseases of Egypt that you feared so much, and you will have no relief.
28.61: The Lord will afflict you with every sickness and plague there is, even those not mentioned in this Book of Instruction, until you are destroyed.
28.62: Though you become as numerous as the stars in the sky, few of you will be left because you would not listen to the Lord your God.
28.63: “Just as the Lord has found great pleasure in causing you to prosper and multiply, the Lord will find pleasure in destroying you. You will be torn from the land you are about to enter and occupy.
28.64: For the Lord will scatter you among all the nations from one end of the earth to the other. There you will worship foreign gods that neither you nor your ancestors have known, gods made of wood and stone!
28.65: There among those nations you will find no peace or place to rest. And the Lord will cause your heart to tremble, your eyesight to fail, and your soul to despair.
28.66: Your life will constantly hang in the balance. You will live night and day in fear, unsure if you will survive.
28.67: In the morning you will say, ‘If only it were night!’ And in the evening you will say, ‘If only it were morning!’ For you will be terrified by the awful horrors you see around you.
28.68: Then the Lord will send you back to Egypt in ships, to a destination I promised you would never see again. There you will offer to sell yourselves to your enemies as slaves, but no one will buy you.”

11.1: “You must love the Lord your God and always obey his requirements, decrees, regulations, and commands.
11.2: Keep in mind that I am not talking now to your children, who have never experienced the discipline of the Lord your God or seen his greatness and his strong hand and powerful arm.
11.3: They didn’t see the miraculous signs and wonders he performed in Egypt against Pharaoh and all his land.
11.4: They didn’t see what the Lord did to the armies of Egypt and to their horses and chariots—how he drowned them in the Red Sea as they were chasing you. He destroyed them, and they have not recovered to this very day!
11.5: “Your children didn’t see how the Lord cared for you in the wilderness until you arrived here.
11.6: They didn’t see what he did to Dathan and Abiram (the sons of Eliab, a descendant of Reuben) when the earth opened its mouth in the Israelite camp and swallowed them, along with their households and tents and every living thing that belonged to them.
11.7: But you have seen the Lord perform all these mighty deeds with your own eyes!
11.8: “Therefore, be careful to obey every command I am giving you today, so you may have strength to go in and take over the land you are about to enter.
11.9: If you obey, you will enjoy a long life in the land the Lord swore to give to your ancestors and to you, their descendants—a land flowing with milk and honey!
11.10: For the land you are about to enter and take over is not like the land of Egypt from which you came, where you planted your seed and made irrigation ditches with your foot as in a vegetable garden.
11.11: Rather, the land you will soon take over is a land of hills and valleys with plenty of rain—
11.12: a land that the Lord your God cares for. He watches over it through each season of the year!
11.13: “If you carefully obey the commands I am giving you today, and if you love the Lord your God and serve him with all your heart and soul,
11.14: then he will send the rains in their proper seasons—the early and late rains—so you can bring in your harvests of grain, new wine, and olive oil.
11.15: He will give you lush pastureland for your livestock, and you yourselves will have all you want to eat.
11.16: “But be careful. Don’t let your heart be deceived so that you turn away from the Lord and serve and worship other gods.
11.17: If you do, the Lord’s anger will burn against you. He will shut up the sky and hold back the rain, and the ground will fail to produce its harvests. Then you will quickly die in that good land the Lord is giving you.
11.18: “So commit yourselves wholeheartedly to these words of mine. Tie them to your hands and wear them on your forehead as reminders.
11.19: Teach them to your children. Talk about them when you are at home and when you are on the road, when you are going to bed and when you are getting up.
11.20: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
11.21: so that as long as the sky remains above the earth, you and your children may flourish in the land the Lord swore to give your ancestors.
11.22: “Be careful to obey all these commands I am giving you. Show love to the Lord your God by walking in his ways and holding tightly to him.
11.23: Then the Lord will drive out all the nations ahead of you, though they are much greater and stronger than you, and you will take over their land.
11.24: Wherever you set foot, that land will be yours. Your frontiers will stretch from the wilderness in the south to Lebanon in the north, and from the Euphrates River in the east to the Mediterranean Sea in the west.
11.25: No one will be able to stand against you, for the Lord your God will cause the people to fear and dread you, as he promised, wherever you go in the whole land.
11.26: “Look, today I am giving you the choice between a blessing and a curse!
11.27: You will be blessed if you obey the commands of the Lord your God that I am giving you today.
11.28: But you will be cursed if you reject the commands of the Lord your God and turn away from him and worship gods you have not known before.
11.29: “When the Lord your God brings you into the land and helps you take possession of it, you must pronounce the blessing at Mount Gerizim and the curse at Mount Ebal.
11.30: (These two mountains are west of the Jordan River in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Jordan Valley, near the town of Gilgal, not far from the oaks of Moreh.)
11.31: For you are about to cross the Jordan River to take over the land the Lord your God is giving you. When you take that land and are living in it,
11.32: you must be careful to obey all the decrees and regulations I am giving you today.

1.1: These are the words that Moses spoke to all the people of Israel while they were in the wilderness east of the Jordan River. They were camped in the Jordan Valley near Suph, between Paran on one side and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Di-zahab on the other.
1.2: Normally it takes only eleven days to travel from Mount Sinai to Kadesh-barnea, going by way of Mount Seir.
1.3: But forty years after the Israelites left Egypt, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses addressed the people of Israel, telling them everything the Lord had commanded him to say.
1.4: This took place after he had defeated King Sihon of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and at Edrei had defeated King Og of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth.
1.5: While the Israelites were in the land of Moab east of the Jordan River, Moses carefully explained the Lord’s instructions as follows.
1.6: “When we were at Mount Sinai, the Lord our God said to us, ‘You have stayed at this mountain long enough.
1.7: It is time to break camp and move on. Go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all the neighboring regions—the Jordan Valley, the hill country, the western foothills, the Negev, and the coastal plain. Go to the land of the Canaanites and to Lebanon, and all the way to the great Euphrates River.
1.8: Look, I am giving all this land to you! Go in and occupy it, for it is the land the Lord swore to give to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to all their descendants.’”
1.9: Moses continued, “At that time I told you, ‘You are too great a burden for me to carry all by myself.
1.10: The Lord your God has increased your population, making you as numerous as the stars!
1.11: And may the Lord, the God of your ancestors, multiply you a thousand times more and bless you as he promised!
1.12: But you are such a heavy load to carry! How can I deal with all your problems and bickering?
1.13: Choose some well-respected men from each tribe who are known for their wisdom and understanding, and I will appoint them as your leaders.’
1.14: “Then you responded, ‘Your plan is a good one.’
1.15: So I took the wise and respected men you had selected from your tribes and appointed them to serve as judges and officials over you. Some were responsible for a thousand people, some for a hundred, some for fifty, and some for ten.
1.16: “At that time I instructed the judges, ‘You must hear the cases of your fellow Israelites and the foreigners living among you. Be perfectly fair in your decisions
1.17: and impartial in your judgments. Hear the cases of those who are poor as well as those who are rich. Don’t be afraid of anyone’s anger, for the decision you make is God’s decision. Bring me any cases that are too difficult for you, and I will handle them.’
1.18: “At that time I gave you instructions about everything you were to do.
1.19: “Then, just as the Lord our God commanded us, we left Mount Sinai and traveled through the great and terrifying wilderness, as you yourselves remember, and headed toward the hill country of the Amorites. When we arrived at Kadesh-barnea,
1.20: I said to you, ‘You have now reached the hill country of the Amorites that the Lord our God is giving us.
1.21: Look! He has placed the land in front of you. Go and occupy it as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, has promised you. Don’t be afraid! Don’t be discouraged!’
1.22: “But you all came to me and said, ‘First, let’s send out scouts to explore the land for us. They will advise us on the best route to take and which towns we should enter.’
1.23: “This seemed like a good idea to me, so I chose twelve scouts, one from each of your tribes.
1.24: They headed for the hill country and came to the valley of Eshcol and explored it.
1.25: They picked some of its fruit and brought it back to us. And they reported, ‘The land the Lord our God has given us is indeed a good land.’
1.26: “But you rebelled against the command of the Lord your God and refused to go in.
1.27: You complained in your tents and said, ‘The Lord must hate us. That’s why he has brought us here from Egypt—to hand us over to the Amorites to be slaughtered.
1.28: Where can we go? Our brothers have demoralized us with their report. They tell us, “The people of the land are taller and more powerful than we are, and their towns are large, with walls rising high into the sky! We even saw giants there—the descendants of Anak!”’
1.29: “But I said to you, ‘Don’t be shocked or afraid of them!
1.30: The Lord your God is going ahead of you. He will fight for you, just as you saw him do in Egypt.
1.31: And you saw how the Lord your God cared for you all along the way as you traveled through the wilderness, just as a father cares for his child. Now he has brought you to this place.’
1.32: “But even after all he did, you refused to trust the Lord your God,
1.33: who goes before you looking for the best places to camp, guiding you with a pillar of fire by night and a pillar of cloud by day.
1.34: “When the Lord heard your complaining, he became very angry. So he solemnly swore,
1.35: ‘Not one of you from this wicked generation will live to see the good land I swore to give your ancestors,
1.36: except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see this land because he has followed the Lord completely. I will give to him and his descendants some of the very land he explored during his scouting mission.’
1.37: “And the Lord was also angry with me because of you. He said to me, ‘Moses, not even you will enter the Promised Land!
1.38: Instead, your assistant, Joshua son of Nun, will lead the people into the land. Encourage him, for he will lead Israel as they take possession of it.
1.39: I will give the land to your little ones—your innocent children. You were afraid they would be captured, but they will be the ones who occupy it.
1.40: As for you, turn around now and go on back through the wilderness toward the Red Sea.’
1.41: “Then you confessed, ‘We have sinned against the Lord! We will go into the land and fight for it, as the Lord our God has commanded us.’ So your men strapped on their weapons, thinking it would be easy to attack the hill country.
1.42: “But the Lord told me to tell you, ‘Do not attack, for I am not with you. If you go ahead on your own, you will be crushed by your enemies.’
1.43: “This is what I told you, but you would not listen. Instead, you again rebelled against the Lord’s command and arrogantly went into the hill country to fight.
1.44: But the Amorites who lived there came out against you like a swarm of bees. They chased and battered you all the way from Seir to Hormah.
1.45: Then you returned and wept before the Lord, but he refused to listen.
1.46: So you stayed there at Kadesh for a long time.

31.1: When Moses had finished giving these instructions to all the people of Israel,
31.2: he said, “I am now 120 years old, and I am no longer able to lead you. The Lord has told me, ‘You will not cross the Jordan River.’
31.3: But the Lord your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy the nations living there, and you will take possession of their land. Joshua will lead you across the river, just as the Lord promised.
31.4: “The Lord will destroy the nations living in the land, just as he destroyed Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites.
31.5: The Lord will hand over to you the people who live there, and you must deal with them as I have commanded you.
31.6: So be strong and courageous! Do not be afraid and do not panic before them. For the Lord your God will personally go ahead of you. He will neither fail you nor abandon you.”
31.7: Then Moses called for Joshua, and as all Israel watched, he said to him, “Be strong and courageous! For you will lead these people into the land that the Lord swore to their ancestors he would give them. You are the one who will divide it among them as their grants of land.
31.8: Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the Lord will personally go ahead of you. He will be with you; he will neither fail you nor abandon you.”
31.9: So Moses wrote this entire body of instruction in a book and gave it to the priests, who carried the Ark of the Lord’s Covenant, and to the elders of Israel.
31.10: Then Moses gave them this command: “At the end of every seventh year, the Year of Release, during the Festival of Shelters,
31.11: you must read this Book of Instruction to all the people of Israel when they assemble before the Lord your God at the place he chooses.
31.12: Call them all together—men, women, children, and the foreigners living in your towns—so they may hear this Book of Instruction and learn to fear the Lord your God and carefully obey all the terms of these instructions.
31.13: Do this so that your children who have not known these instructions will hear them and will learn to fear the Lord your God. Do this as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to occupy.”
31.14: Then the Lord said to Moses, “The time has come for you to die. Call Joshua and present yourselves at the Tabernacle, so that I may commission him there.” So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the Tabernacle.
31.15: And the Lord appeared to them in a pillar of cloud that stood at the entrance to the sacred tent.
31.16: The Lord said to Moses, “You are about to die and join your ancestors. After you are gone, these people will begin to worship foreign gods, the gods of the land where they are going. They will abandon me and break my covenant that I have made with them.
31.17: Then my anger will blaze forth against them. I will abandon them, hiding my face from them, and they will be devoured. Terrible trouble will come down on them, and on that day they will say, ‘These disasters have come down on us because God is no longer among us!’
31.18: At that time I will hide my face from them on account of all the evil they commit by worshiping other gods.
31.19: “So write down the words of this song, and teach it to the people of Israel. Help them learn it, so it may serve as a witness for me against them.
31.20: For I will bring them into the land I swore to give their ancestors—a land flowing with milk and honey. There they will become prosperous, eat all the food they want, and become fat. But they will begin to worship other gods; they will despise me and break my covenant.
31.21: And when great disasters come down on them, this song will stand as evidence against them, for it will never be forgotten by their descendants. I know the intentions of these people, even now before they have entered the land I swore to give them.”
31.22: So that very day Moses wrote down the words of the song and taught it to the Israelites.
31.23: Then the Lord commissioned Joshua son of Nun with these words: “Be strong and courageous, for you must bring the people of Israel into the land I swore to give them. I will be with you.”
31.24: When Moses had finished writing this entire body of instruction in a book,
31.25: he gave this command to the Levites who carried the Ark of the Lord’s Covenant:
31.26: “Take this Book of Instruction and place it beside the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord your God, so it may remain there as a witness against the people of Israel.
31.27: For I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. Even now, while I am still alive and am here with you, you have rebelled against the Lord. How much more rebellious will you be after my death!
31.28: “Now summon all the elders and officials of your tribes, so that I can speak to them directly and call heaven and earth to witness against them.
31.29: I know that after my death you will become utterly corrupt and will turn from the way I have commanded you to follow. In the days to come, disaster will come down on you, for you will do what is evil in the Lord’s sight, making him very angry with your actions.”
31.30: So Moses recited this entire song publicly to the assembly of Israel:

27.1: Then Moses and the leaders of Israel gave this charge to the people: “Obey all these commands that I am giving you today.
27.2: When you cross the Jordan River and enter the land the Lord your God is giving you, set up some large stones and coat them with plaster.
27.3: Write this whole body of instruction on them when you cross the river to enter the land the Lord your God is giving you—a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, promised you.
27.4: When you cross the Jordan, set up these stones at Mount Ebal and coat them with plaster, as I am commanding you today.
27.5: “Then build an altar there to the Lord your God, using natural, uncut stones. You must not shape the stones with an iron tool.
27.6: Build the altar of uncut stones, and use it to offer burnt offerings to the Lord your God.
27.7: Also sacrifice peace offerings on it, and celebrate by feasting there before the Lord your God.
27.8: You must clearly write all these instructions on the stones coated with plaster.”
27.9: Then Moses and the Levitical priests addressed all Israel as follows: “O Israel, be quiet and listen! Today you have become the people of the Lord your God.
27.10: So you must obey the Lord your God by keeping all these commands and decrees that I am giving you today.”
27.11: That same day Moses also gave this charge to the people:
27.12: “When you cross the Jordan River, the tribes of Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin must stand on Mount Gerizim to proclaim a blessing over the people.
27.13: And the tribes of Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali must stand on Mount Ebal to proclaim a curse.
27.14: “Then the Levites will shout to all the people of Israel:
27.15: ‘Cursed is anyone who carves or casts an idol and secretly sets it up. These idols, the work of craftsmen, are detestable to the Lord.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.16: ‘Cursed is anyone who dishonors father or mother.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.17: ‘Cursed is anyone who steals property from a neighbor by moving a boundary marker.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.18: ‘Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person astray on the road.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.19: ‘Cursed is anyone who denies justice to foreigners, orphans, or widows.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.20: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sexual intercourse with one of his father’s wives, for he has violated his father.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.21: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sexual intercourse with an animal.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.22: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sexual intercourse with his sister, whether she is the daughter of his father or his mother.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.23: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sexual intercourse with his mother-in-law.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.24: ‘Cursed is anyone who attacks a neighbor in secret.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
27.25: ‘Cursed is anyone who accepts payment to kill an innocent person.’ And all the people will reply, ‘Amen.’
